lines.display: *Last* *time:* a railway built a department store inside its own *station*.
lines.spoken: Last time: a railway built a department store inside its own station.

lines.display: Its first shop staff?
lines.spoken: Its first shop staff?

lines.display: *Railwaymen* who had been *driving* its *trains*.
lines.spoken: Railwaymen who had been driving its trains.

lines.display: Hankyu's boss, *Kobayashi* *Ichizō*, saw big stores spending *fortunes* to lure shoppers
lines.spoken: Hahn-cue's boss, Kobayashi Ee-chee-zoh, saw big stores spending fortunes to lure shoppers

lines.display: with *ads*, free *delivery* and *shuttle* *buses*.
lines.spoken: with ads, free delivery and shuttle buses.

lines.display: His station brought *crowds* *every* *day*.
lines.spoken: His station brought crowds every day.

lines.display: First he *tested* it, renting a floor of his Umeda building to an established store
lines.spoken: First he tested it, renting a floor of his Oo-meh-da building to an established store

lines.display: and *watching* it sell.
lines.spoken: and watching it sell.

lines.display: When the lease ended in *1925*, Hankyu *took* *over*,
lines.spoken: When the lease ended in nineteen twenty-five, Hahn-cue took over,

lines.display: even advertising for *wholesalers* to tell its *amateurs* what to stock.
lines.spoken: even advertising for wholesalers to tell its amateurs what to stock.

lines.display: On *April* *15th,* *1929*, Hankyu opened an *eight-storey* building at Umeda Station:
lines.spoken: On April fifteenth, nineteen twenty-nine, Hahn-cue opened an eight-storey building at Oo-meh-da Station:

lines.display: the *concourse* at street level, *shop* *floors* above, *dining* *halls* on top.
lines.spoken: the concourse at street level, shop floors above, dining halls on top.

lines.display: Its promise: the *best* *goods*, *cheaper* than anywhere.
lines.spoken: Its promise: the best goods, cheaper than anywhere.

lines.display: The dining halls *paid* for the bargains.
lines.spoken: The dining halls paid for the bargains.

lines.display: Curry rice cost *25* *sen*,
lines.spoken: Curry rice cost twenty-five sen,

lines.display: and in *1931* Kobayashi cut prices again:
lines.spoken: and in nineteen thirty-one Kobayashi cut prices again:

lines.display: *half* *a* *sen* of profit per plate, he said, was enough.
lines.spoken: half a sen of profit per plate, he said, was enough.

lines.display: *Legend* says that when other stores turned away *rice-only* orders,
lines.spoken: Legend says that when other stores turned away rice-only orders,

lines.display: Hankyu *welcomed* them.
lines.spoken: Hahn-cue welcomed them.

lines.display: Tokyo followed in *1934*, when *Gotō* *Keita's* railway opened a terminal store at *Shibuya*;
lines.spoken: Tokyo followed in nineteen thirty-four, when Go-toh Kay-ta's railway opened a terminal store at Shibuya;

lines.display: Gotō credited the idea to *Kobayashi*.
lines.spoken: Go-toh credited the idea to Kobayashi.

lines.display: By *1936*, Hankyu's building wrapped around Umeda Station like a *horseshoe*.
lines.spoken: By nineteen thirty-six, Hahn-cue's building wrapped around Oo-meh-da Station like a horseshoe.

lines.display: And in *1930*, a Tokyo department-store dining hall
lines.spoken: And in nineteen thirty, a Tokyo department-store dining hall

lines.display: shaped rice into a tiny *Mount* *Fuji* and planted a *flag* on top.
lines.spoken: shaped rice into a tiny Mount Fuji and planted a flag on top.
